COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
11.09.2025 C 528 No.1563 of 2025
Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
This Application has been filed for 
quashing the entire proceedings of Criminal 
Case No.2399 of 2024, pending before the 
court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dehradun 
under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 
Section 120B of the Indian Penal Code, 
1860.
2. Heard Mr. Neeraj Garg, learned 
counsel for the applicants and Mr. Pradeep 
Lohani, learned Brief Holder for the 
respondent no.1.
3. Mr. Pradeep Lohani, Brief Holder has 
sought three weeks’ time to file counter 
affidavit in the present fresh matter. 
4. Time is granted. 
5. Notice is being issued to the 
respondent no.2. Steps to be taken within 
three days.
6. List on 09.10.2025.
 (Alok Kumar Verma, J.)

Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
1. Ms. Suraiya Naaz, learned counsel for the 
applicant.
2. Mr. Anchit Khokher, learned counsel for the 
applicant in connected C528 No. 713 of 2025.
3. Mr. Rajendra Arya, learned counsel holding the 
brief of Mr. Neeraj Garg, learned counsel for the 
applicant in the connected C528 No. 1563 of 2025.
4. Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned A.G.A. with Mrs. 
Shweta Badola Dobhal, learned Brief Holder for the 
State.
5. In C528 No. 713 of 2025 the two chargesheets are 
enclosed; one at page 145 and other one at page 177. The 
charge-sheet, which is enclosed at page 145 reflects that 
there is an endorsement of learned Chief Judicial 
Magistrate, Dehradun, for taking cognizance on this  charge-sheet for the offences punishable under sections 
420, 406 and 120 B of IPC and the last page of this 
charge-sheet reveals that it was cancelled on 21.03.2023.
Page 170 also reveals that the charge-sheet was 
forwarded by the S.H.O. at P.S. Prem Nagar on 
18.04.2022.
6. The another charge-sheet is at page 177 and it was 
forwarded on 11.04.2023, wherein, learned Judicial 
Magistrate, Dehradun, took cognizance for the offences 
punishable under sections 406, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 
120B of IPC.
7. Now, in this petition the proceeding is being 
challenged that from these two charge-sheets it reveals 
that the subsequent charge-sheet is the outcome of re￾investigation, though as per the Rules the re￾investigation is not permissible and the second charge￾sheet does not reveal that it is a supplementary charge￾sheet.
8. It is submitted that once the charge-sheet is filed 
there is no any question to file another charge-sheet 
particularly when in the first charge-sheet the learned 
Chief Judicial Magistrate already took cognizance. 
9. Apart from this, in C528 No. 1010 of 2026 the Trial 
Court submitted a detail report that the persons, who are 
chargesheeted are not joining the Trial Court proceeding 
and though the charge-sheet was filed in the year 2024 
but uptill date the charges has not been framed. In 
connected C528 petition the Trial Court proceeding is 
not stayed, therefore, in such an eventuality avoiding the 
Trial Court proceeding by the accused persons on one 
pretext to another is wholly unwarranted. It has been 
apprised that before the Trial Court 30.09.2026 is fixed, 
therefore, the applicants of the connected C528 petition 
shall ensure their presence on the date fixed before the 
Trial Court so that the Trial Court may proceed.
10. The Registry may get the report from the 
concerned Trial Court about these two charge-sheets, 
which are enclosed at page 145 and 177.
11. In addition to this, Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned 
A.G.A. may also get the instructions from the concerned 
Investigating Officer about these two charge-sheets.
12. Put up this matter on 30.09.2026.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 22.09.2026
PR

Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
1. Mr. Lalit Sharma and Ms. Suraiya Naaz, learned 
counsel for the applicant.
2. Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned A.G.A. with Mrs. 
Sweta Badola Dobhal, learned Brief Holder for the 
State.
3. Mr. Anchit Khokher, learned counsel for the 
respondent.
4. The Trial Court submitted its detailed report in 
compliance of the previous order, wherein, it is 
reported that the two accused persons namely 
Ramkumar Tyagi and Rajkumar Tyagi are avoiding 
the Trial Court proceeding, therefore, warrant have 
been issued against them for securing their presence 
and the next date fixed before the Trial Court is 
29.10.2026. The other accused persons are Ramnaresh 
Tyagi, Avneet Tyagi and Rakesh Tyagi are the 
applicants in C528 No. 713 of 2025 and Karan Singh, 
Vijay Kumar and Deepak Kumar, who are the 
applicants of C528 No. 1563 of 2025 are directed to 
ensure their presence before the Trial Court since as 
apprised to this court the charges has yet not been  framed though there is no order regarding stay of the 
proceeding. In such a situation when there is no stay 
on the ongoing proceeding avoiding the Trial Court 
proceeding is unwarranted and, in such an 
eventuality, all the accused persons should ensure 
their presence before the Trial Court. The Trial Court 
also submitted earlier report and after perusing the 
same it reveals that the accused persons are 
deliberately avoiding the Trial Court proceeding. 
5. It has also been apprised that one of the accused 
person Ramkumar Tyagi is at present 90 years old
then, in such an eventuality, he has a liberty to move
an exemption application to appear through the 
counsel at the time of framing of charge by ensuring 
his presence through V.C. but in any manner the Trial 
Court proceeding cannot avoided.
6. C528 No. 1010 of 2026 is moved only for 
expediting the Trial Court proceeding since the Trial 
Court taking all efforts to expedite the trial, therefore, 
there is no useful purpose to keep this matter pending. 
Accordingly, the proceeding of C528 No. 1010 of 2026
is closed at this stage.
7. Since, the C528 No. 1010 of 2026 is closed, 
therefore, the Registry is directed to tag both the 
reports of Trial Court dated 10.09.2026 and 30.09.2026 
with C528 No. 713 of 2025.
8. In reference to the two chargesheets wherein the 
Trial Court took cognizance Mr. Tumul Nainwal, 
learned A.G.A., on instructions submits that in the first 
chargesheet there was no cognizance since without 
placing the chargesheet before the Trial Court the 
S.S.P. concerned ordered for further investigation and 
due to some inadvertence there is a seal of the 
concerned court in the first chargesheet, however, for 
clarifying this position the prosecution will move an 
appropriate application before the Trial Court within 
ten days so that there may not be doubt on this. He
also submits that the Trial Court proceeding is going 
on only in the subsequent chargesheet dated 
11.04.2023.
9. In C528 No. 713 of 2025 pleadings are 
exchanged. In C528 NO. 1563 of 2025 the counter 
affidavit has not been filed. Respondents are directed 
to file their counter affidavit within three weeks.
10. One week thereafter is granted to the applicant 
to file rejoinder affidavit.
11. List this matter in the week commencing  07.12.2026.
12. It is made clear that since the Trial Court 
proceedings are not stayed the Trial Court may 
proceed with the matter since the trial court 
proceeding are pending since 2024 but charges has not 
been framed as yet. All the accused persons are 
directed to ensure their presence before the trial court 
on the next date fixed.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 08.10.2026
